  "Id~SEC-"` gives 15, as Docs/TestPlan.md claims. The count arithmetic checks
  out: 165 + 162 + 37 = 364, the category table sums to 209 IDs, and Tests.Api
  is 199.

  No High findings. One Medium and four Low.

  MEDIUM

  M1. SEC-014 can pass when the property it guards is broken.
  - Where: tests/TechOneNumberToWordsApp.Tests/Api/StaticFilesApiTests.cs:50-58,
  with src/TechOneNumberToWordsApp.Web/wwwroot/app.js:3.
  - The positive check is `Assert.Contains("textContent", script)`. app.js line
  3 is a comment that contains the word "textContent" ("...with textContent,
  never as markup (D24)"). Someone could replace every `textContent =` in the
  code with some other insertion path, and the comment alone would keep that
  assertion green.
  - The test's own comment says the scan includes comments, so it knows comments
  count. It uses that only for the forbidden words.
  - The forbidden list is a short blocklist, so these all pass the scan:
    - `setHTMLUnsafe`, `parseHTMLUnsafe`, `Range.createContextualFragment`,
  `DOMParser`, `eval` and `new Function`
    - `element['inner' + 'HTML']`
    - `setAttribute('srcdoc', ...)`
  - TestPlan.md line 133 says "contains `textContent`" and section 5.5 says
  "checks that it uses `textContent`". Both overstate what is checked.
  - Fix, either of:
    - Strengthen the positive check to match code, for example
  `Assert.Matches(@"\.textContent\s*=", script)`. Both uses in app.js (lines 104
  and 106 of the file; lines 80-81 in the diff numbering) match that pattern.
    - Keep the check as is and reword the TestPlan and D24 text to say it is
  only a blocklist plus "the word appears".
  - Optionally add `HTMLUnsafe`, `createContextualFragment`, `DOMParser`,
  `eval(` and `new Function` to the list. The limit is already documented as
  "cannot prove safety", so this is a matter of honesty and strength, not a bug.

  LOW

  L1. The focus outline has weak contrast against the page background.
  - Where: wwwroot/site.css lines 215-219 (`outline: 3px solid #f2a900`).
  - #f2a900 on white is about 2.0:1. WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 asks for 3:1 for a focus
  indicator, and D5/UI-015 cite accessibility basics. UI-015 only checks that
  the outline is "visible", so a manual pass would not catch it.
  - Fix: use a darker outline such as #b36b00 or #1a4f8b, or a two-colour
  outline.

  L2. "Converting…" is probably not announced to screen readers.
  - Where: wwwroot/app.js lines 124-125 and 140.
  - `aria-busy="true"` is set on the live region at the same moment
  "Converting…" is written into it. Most screen readers suppress announcements
  from a busy live region.
  - The plan's stated reason for the text (item 3: a slow request "would say
  nothing to a screen reader") is therefore probably not achieved. D5 and E6
  only say the box shows "Converting…", so this is not a log violation.
  - Fix: drop `aria-busy` (the button's disabled state and the text already
  carry the state), or accept the behaviour and say so. Worth a look when the
  author does UI-015 with a screen reader. It is unverified here because no
  browser was run.

  L3. Browser-compatibility risk: `AbortSignal.timeout` is a hard dependency.
  - Where: wwwroot/app.js line 65, inside the `try`.
  - On a browser without `AbortSignal.timeout` (Safari before 16, Chrome before
  124, Firefox before 100) it throws a TypeError. The `catch` turns that into
  the generic fallback, so every conversion fails with "Something went wrong"
  and the page looks broken, not degraded.
  - Only the D60 form is specified, and the target is modern Chrome, so this may
  be acceptable. I suggest recording it in TestPlan 5.5 or Readme section 10
  (Limitations), which already say only Chrome is checked. A guarded fallback
  would be `typeof AbortSignal.timeout === 'function' ? ... : undefined`, but
  that is a design choice for the author.

  L4. SEC-005 does not prove the pipeline ordering that the D34 amendment
  states.
  - Where: StaticFilesApiTests.cs lines 23-36 and the D34 amendment text.
  - The amendment says static files sit after the HTTPS redirect and the
  exception handler. The test uses an https client, so it cannot detect static
  files moved before `UseHttpsRedirection` or before `UseExceptionHandler`. It
  does catch the important regression of moving them before
  `UseSecurityHeaders`.
  - This is acceptable, because the plan's own SEC-005 scope is "same headers
  and media type". Just do not read it as covering D35 for the page. UI-018
  covers the redirect by hand.

  L5. Focus is pulled to Convert whenever `activeElement` is the body.
  - Where: wwwroot/app.js lines 136-138.
  - If the user deliberately clicks on blank page space during a request (focus
  goes to the body), focus is moved to Convert when the request ends. This is
  minor. It is the documented behaviour: E6 says "if focus was lost... it
  returns to Convert", and the code comment says "Not when focus is somewhere
  else on purpose". The body check cannot distinguish "lost" from "clicked the
  page background". No change needed unless the author cares.

  CHECKED AND FINE
  - Pipeline order in Program.cs: security headers, HSTS (not Development),
  https redirect, exception handler (not Development), `UseDefaultFiles`,
  `UseStaticFiles`, status code pages, then the endpoint. It matches the D34,
  D35 and D38 amendments and option A in the plan. `UseDefaultFiles` is before
  `UseStaticFiles`. API-010 (404 ProblemDetails) is still green. The comments
  are accurate.
  - The CSP in D34 against all four files:
    - index.html has no inline script, `<style>`, `style=` or `on*=` handler. It
  loads `/site.css`, `/app.js` (deferred) and `/favicon.svg` from the same
  origin.
    - site.css has no `@import`, `url()` or external font.
    - favicon.svg has no script or external reference.
    - app.js has no `eval` and no dynamic script creation.
    - There is no inline style anywhere. `className` is used, not `style`.
  - D6: no `maxlength`, `required` or `pattern`, no trimming, and the raw
  `input.value` is sent.
  - D5:
    - The label is tied to the input with `for`/`id`. The hint is tied with
  `aria-describedby`.
    - `type=text`, `inputmode=decimal`, `autocomplete=off`. `lang=en-AU`.
    - The output is `role=status`, `aria-live=polite`, `aria-atomic=true`, never
  hidden, and starts with no whitespace so `:empty` works.
    - The error label is its own element, and the error border is heavier, so it
  is not shown by colour alone.
    - There is no `noscript`, as decided.
  - D24 response rule matches exactly:
    - 2xx with a string `words` shows the words.
    - A 500 always shows the fallback, plus Reference only if `traceId` is a
  non-empty string.
    - Otherwise a non-empty string `detail`, else the fallback.
    - The body is parsed inside a try whatever the content type.
    - A null, array or non-string field is handled by `field()`.
    - An abort during `response.json()` is also caught.
    - All server text goes in via `textContent`.
  - D60: `AbortSignal.timeout(15000)` is in the options argument of `fetch`, so
  UI-019 can work. A timeout and a network failure both give the plain fallback
  with no Reference.
  - E6:
    - The busy guard returns early on a second submit.
    - The button is disabled and the field is `readOnly`, not disabled.
    - The old result is replaced by "Converting…".
    - The `finally` always undoes busy, `disabled` and `readOnly`.
    - Focus is restored only after the button is re-enabled, which is the right
  order. Enter in the read-only field submits but is ignored by the guard.
    - `aria-busy` is removed before the answer is written. `convert()` never
  throws.
  - Static-file behaviour: a path with no file still gives the 404
  ProblemDetails. The Web package has no new dependencies. No `Cache-Control` is
  set, as decided.
  - Tests: the SEC-005 theory asserts 200, the media type and the exact headers
  (each present once) on all four files. If static files were moved ahead of the
  security-headers middleware, the theory would fail. The second guard,
  `Assert.Equal(HttpStatusCode.OK, ...)` in SEC-014, stops the test passing on a
  404 body. The factory is a class fixture, and the clients and responses are
  in `using`. The refactor into `SecurityHeadersAssert` is behaviour-preserving,
  with the expected values moved verbatim. Traits match the TestPlan: SEC-005
  has D34, D38 and C3, and SEC-014 has D24.
  - Docs against code:
    - The counts, IDs and file names in the Readme and TestPlan are correct. The
  commit claim is right: `74855e3` is the last code commit and HEAD is docs
  only.
    - The 19 UI cases match the plan's final table word for word, with an empty
  Outcome column (as expected).
    - The "no automated JS tests" statement (5.5), the traceability table, the
  "IDs not used" list (SEC-013) and the D47 amendment are consistent.
    - The Readme claims (the launch profile opens the page, 15 s timeout,
  Reference, the files in wwwroot, headers on the page's files, the section
  references) are correct.
    - DesignDecisions amendments were appended and nothing was deleted. The new
  D60 row is present, the document map has the 02- and 03- AI files, and the
  files exist in Docs/AI.
  - Nothing implemented but not logged: the favicon and C3, the 15 s timeout
  (D60), the "Error:" label and the focus return (E6 amendment) are all logged.
  Every logged slice-10 decision is implemented.

      135  | D43 | Conversion cases live in an **external JSON file** (`t
           ests/.../TestData/conversion-cases.json`). Row: `id`, `decisio
           ns[]`, `description`, `input`, and either `expectedWords` or `
           expectedErrorCode` (+ optional `messageContains`). A **self-va
           lidating loader** (System.Text.Json, no package) fails the run
            on a duplicate ID, a row with both or neither expectation, or
            an `expectedErrorCode` that isn't a real enum member. Tests t
           ake only the case ID and look the row up. HTTP and behaviour c
           hecks (E5, missing body/amount, 415/404/405, 500, security hea
           ders, 413) stay as ordinary C# tests | Example row: `{ "id": "
           AND-003", "decisions": ["D8"], "description": "No AND between 
           large groups", "input": "1,000,100", "expectedWords": "ONE MIL
           LION ONE HUNDRED DOLLARS" }`. Rejected: `[InlineData]` / `Theo
           ryData` (data mixed into code, invisible characters easy to mi
           ss, weak fit with the brief's "test data"); CSV (inputs contai
           n commas so every input needs quoting; no built-in .NET CSV re
           ader; no escape syntax for NBSP/tab/emoji; Excel silently chan
           ges data — "007"→7, ".5"→0.5, "1e5"→100000). **Setup note (sli
           ce 0):** the loader's check that `expectedErrorCode` is a real
            enum member is added once the error-code enum exists. **Setup
            note (slice 2):** the loader also rejects unknown JSON fields
            (`UnmappedMemberHandling.Disallow`), so a misspelt field like
            `messageContain` fails the run instead of being ignored, and 
           rejects rows with an empty decisions list. **Amended (slice 8a
           ):** lone-surrogate inputs can't be written in JSON, so they'r
           e a C# test (VAL-021) with Id and Decision traits. IDs are sha
           red across the JSON file and C# tests, so the next VAL row in 
           the JSON starts at VAL-022. **Amended (gate 1):** the loader a
           lso rejects explicit nulls in fields that can't be null (`Resp
           ectNullableAnnotations`), with the row's position in the messa
           ge | Agreed (amended) |

           rCode` + title "Invalid amount") | Proves the layers agree, an

           les (two sources of truth). **Amended (slice 9):** each row al
           so checks the response content type (`application/json` for 20
           0, `application/problem+json` for 400) and, for rejections, th
           at `detail` contains the row's `messageContains` | Agreed (ame
           nded) |
